# DECISIONS.md — World 001, step 1

Short decision records. Newest at the bottom. Proposals wait for the founder; decisions are marked as such.

---

## D-001 — Replaceability statement (copied from v1 §24, which spec §1 says applies unchanged)

**Code generated by Fable is an experiment, not a Hunt architecture commitment.**

World 001 selects no engine, renderer, schema, provider, or production pipeline for The Hunt. Any later adoption follows ADR-0011: a benchmark, a new ADR, and the founder's approval. The lasting Hunt format stays the Hunt-owned World Package. It is never "Fable output".

**Three.js placeholder record:**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Why selected | A light, MIT-licensed, widely supported WebGL2 library. It is the library the builder model has the most public evidence of using well. For this experiment, a smaller correction effort for an AI builder is a Hunt-specific requirement. |
| Limitations | No built-in game framework, physics, navigation, or XR-ready interaction layer. More must be assembled by hand. Phone performance depends on our own discipline. |
| Preferred future solution | Unknown. Earlier research names Babylon.js as the provisional lead for an interaction-heavy 3D room, with PlayCanvas as the comparator. That needs a benchmark. |
| What depends on it | `src/render/`, `src/player/`, and parts of `src/gen/`. Not `src/world/` (data) and not `src/game/` (rules, the judge). |
| Replaceability class | Easy for this experiment. Moderate if the code is reused. |
| Migration path | Keep the world data and the rules free of renderer code. Rewrite the render, player, and generator layers against the same data. |
| Estimated replacement cost | Roughly half the code, mostly rendering and generators *(estimate, low confidence)*. |
| Replacement triggers | T1 or T2 cannot be met; XR or physics needs that Three.js handles poorly; or a benchmark shows a clearly better engine for Hunt worlds. |

## D-004 — Trust rules as code structure (decision, spec §6)

One judge module (`src/game/judge.ts`) makes every "is this found?" decision. All answer data lives in `src/world/answers.json`, read only by the judge, marked "to move server-side before any prize hunt". The session log stays. No debug shortcut ships in the playtest build. Accounts, bot checks, guess limits and hashes are not in step 1.

## D-006 — Founder decision at STOP 0 (2026-09-29): all nine proposals accepted

The founder accepted all nine proposals in `PLAN.md` §1. They are now decisions. `SOLUTIONS.md` stands as written; its fallbacks no longer apply.

**One change to proposal 4 (founder's words):** the "getting warm" feedback must also respond to zoom. A player facing the right direction at the wrong zoom must still see the sketch lines start to line up. So warmth is computed from both the angle and the zoom distance to the stored pose. The judge returns one warmth value in 0..1; the angle term and the zoom term each contribute, and the lock still needs both to be within their bands for 0.8 s.

**Phase 0 cost, from the founder:** $10 (credit balance $250 → $240). Recorded in `PRODUCTION_LOG.md`.

**Phase A budget rule, from the founder:** stop and report if Phase A reaches about $60, even if it is not finished. Keep the graybox simple: plain shapes, no art.

## D-007 — Input conventions and the lens hold (decision in the graybox, spec §4 leaves them open)

- **Look:** the world follows the finger or mouse. Drag right to look left, drag down to look up. Arrow keys turn at about 70° per second at 1×, slower when zoomed. Sensitivity 0.18° per pixel at 1×, divided by the zoom.
- **Lens:** wheel and pinch set a zoom level that stays. Holding the lens (the button, the right mouse button, or Z) zooms toward 4× in about a second and eases back to the set level on release. This gives phones a one-finger zoom, and it is the same hold that fills the dive ring.
- **Dive trigger:** the ring fills while an active dive target is centered and the lens is held, or the zoom is 1.5× or more. Tapping, clicking, E or Enter on a centered dive target starts the dive at once (the accessibility path in spec §4).
- **Verbs:** the crosshair picks the nearest usable thing within its angular size or 22 px, whichever is bigger. A hidden object is picked only when the judge would accept a find there (right viewpoint, centered, zoomed enough).
- **Escape** closes any open panel; with nothing open it opens the menu. Tab is never used.
- **Two viewpoints per place** are ordinary objects with the verb "Stand here". The glide takes about 0.9 s and resets the zoom.

## D-008 — Gate A result (founder, 2026-09-29): redesign once

**What happened.** The founder played blind on a laptop. He never found a dive and did not find the second viewpoint. He thought the locked shop door was broken, because nothing showed it was locked or that a key existed. He could not turn around and could not tell what can be zoomed into. He zoomed on the moon in the sky and expected it to lead somewhere. He read the top bar as a menu.

**Decision:** redesign once (spec §13 S1, first of the one allowed redesign). No art yet. The next round after this one is a single street style frame.

**The eight changes, in the founder's order:**
1. Full 360° turning at every viewpoint. Up/down limits stay.
2. Moving: 3–5 stand spots per place. Tap or click a spot on the ground, or use the keys toward it, and the camera glides there at a fixed speed. Spots are faint marks that brighten under the crosshair. No free walking.
3. Show what can be entered: the next place must be visible inside its dive target before the dive. The crosshair changes only over things you can act on; plain scenery gives no reaction. The moon in the street sky must not react or look like a target.
4. After 45 seconds of no input, the most useful next thing glints once. No text.
5. Locked things show it without words: a rattle plus a small keyhole mark.
6. The dive is one continuous forward zoom through the target into the next place, with no visible cut. If the seam cannot be hidden, report it rather than fake it.
7. The top bar shows only places already reached; later ones are dots. It must not look clickable. It must not run under the buttons on phones.
8. "Download log" becomes "Copy log". Downloads are blocked where the game is hosted.

**Budget for this round:** stop and report when 1–8 are done, or at $50 spent, whichever comes first. The credit balance in the founder's message was left as a placeholder ("[balance]"), so no figure is recorded.

**How they are built (builder's notes):**
- Yaw is now measured in world terms at every spot (all headings are 0), so a player keeps facing the same way when moving between spots. Data that was written relative to a turned viewpoint was converted once.
- Spots are generated from `places.json` viewpoints; they are no longer listed in `objects.json`.
- Hidden objects are judged from the object's position and the player's current spot, so a hidden thing can be found from any spot it is centered from, with the zoom needed scaled by distance. Sketches stay bound to the spot they were drawn from.
- Change 3 and change 6 share one mechanism: a portal. The next place is rendered live from an "approach" camera into a texture shown on the dive target's opening (and on the shop window). The dive flies the camera to that opening until the opening fills the screen, then hands over to the real next place with the same camera, so the two images match at the hand-over.
- Keys: arrow keys still look (spec §4 keyboard-only play needs a look key). W, A, S, D move toward the nearest spot in that direction. E or Enter on a spot under the crosshair also moves.

## D-009 — Second play (founder, 2026-09-29): free walking, a teaching first place, real-input proof

**What happened.** The founder played the redesigned graybox and still could not move or reach the shop. The founder then tested the playtest build directly: clicking a stand ring did nothing; only W moved. The end-to-end tests had missed it because they moved through debug hooks, not real clicks.

**Root cause, found by the builder with real mouse events:** the ring was drawn and hit-tested as a thin annulus (the line of the ring, 12 cm wide, seen from up to 8 m away). A click inside the ring, where a person naturally clicks, hit the ground and did nothing. The one end-to-end test that "clicked" a ring did so through a hook at the exact crosshair, so it never saw the miss.

**The founder's changes, in order:**
1. Free walking inside each place replaces stand rings. Tap or click anywhere on the ground and the player walks there at a fixed speed; W A S D walk on a keyboard. Walls, furniture and edges block movement. Hidden objects and sketches must stay fair from any reachable position; the builder reports any that become unfair.
2. From now on, a feature counts as working only if an end-to-end test reaches it with real clicks or taps on the playtest build. Hooks may set up a test, never prove it.
3. Place 1 becomes a teaching place. The shop door stands open from the start, with the lit shop and the cat visible inside. The first dive must be possible within 60 seconds. The key-and-door puzzle moves to place 2 or is dropped; the builder says which.
4. Place 1 keeps at most 6 ordinary usable things. Decoys may return from place 2 onward.
5. The start screen shows three things, with pictures and very few words: drag to look; tap the ground to walk; hold the lens on a glowing opening to go in.
6. One end-to-end test plays place 1 like a new player, on the playtest build, with real clicks only: start, walk, dive into the shop, within 60 seconds of game time.
7. Check whether this container can download files from polyhaven.com, kenney.nl and quaternius.com. Report yes or no for each. No art yet.

**Budget for this round:** stop and report when done, or at $35 spent.

**Builder decisions inside these changes:**
- **The key puzzle moved to place 2, not dropped.** The blue drawer in the shop is locked (keyhole mark, rattle); the key lies on the counter by the door. Reasons: every place after the first keeps one required open-or-use step, as spec §3 asks; the locked-thing marks from D-008 stay in use; and the shop's step now also teaches walking (counter first, chest second). The street has no required step, so the count of finds keeps 24 by counting each dive as a find (6 sketches, 12 hidden things, 6 dives) instead of each completed place.
- **Taps: near the crosshair they act, elsewhere they walk.** A tap or click within 22% of the short screen side from the centre acts on what the crosshair shows; any other tap walks to the tapped ground. E and Enter always act. So the founder's phone taps "when a verb shows" keep working, and a tap on the ground is never swallowed by a verb.
- **Blocking is derived from the world data**, not hand-drawn: every solid prop or object whose height overlaps the player's body (above the knee, below the head) blocks, kept one body radius away; rotated boxes use their true outline; scattered dressing of more than 40 pieces (cobbles, stars, fur) never blocks; thin hairs and whiskers are marked not solid; hills and the moon's rise are platforms that raise the floor. Each place lists its walkable zones (rectangles or a disc) in `places.json`. Openings are walls: you dive through them, never walk.
- **Sketches lock from a position, not a spot name:** within a per-sketch distance of the spot they were drawn from (`posTol` in `answers.json`, 0.8 to 15 place units). "Getting warm" fades to zero by three times that distance, so a player facing the right way from the wrong place sees faint lines and knows to move.
- **A hidden thing must be in sight.** The crosshair now offers a hidden object only if some part of it can be seen from the eye (rays to its centre and corners). This exposed five hidden objects that were buried inside their host shapes in the graybox (the umbrella inside the fish stall, the teacup behind the shop wall, the marble and the moon footprint under the floor, the moon stamp inside the stamp tower). They were only ever "found" by pointing at a box. All five were moved into view; a unit test now checks every hidden object is in sight from the spot its hints describe. The blue drawer fronts were also inside the chest and are now proud of it.
- **Named spots stay in the data** as authoring anchors (objects are placed relative to them), as dive arrival points, as the sketch positions, and for "describe surroundings" (the nearest spot's text). The player never sees them.
- **The dive prefers the glowing opening.** With the door open from the start, the street had two openings into the shop; the seam check caught the dive flying through the window and past the sleeping cat.
- **Saves from before this round are discarded** (save version 2), since they hold a spot name instead of a position.

**Download check (change 7):** polyhaven.com, api.polyhaven.com, dl.polyhaven.org, kenney.nl and quaternius.com all answer "CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403" from the container's proxy. **No for all three sites.** Any asset from them would have to be fetched by the founder and added to the repository with its licence recorded in `PROVENANCE.md`.

## D-010 — Fourth round (founder, 2026-09-30): direction A realistic, one street style frame, guidance, dependency chart

**Founder decisions.** Art direction A, realistic. Assets: the branch `assets/polyhaven-street-shop` (33 CC0 Poly Haven assets fetched by the build lead, since this container cannot reach asset hosts), merged into the working branch. Three parts: (1) one realistic style frame of the street only, with HDRI light and sky, shadows, tone mapping, mist, PBR textures, real depth on the houses, glTF models where they fit, simple water, game logic unchanged, the seam check still passing, only the street's assets loaded, download size and phone frame rate reported, a lower tier if needed, the cat simple, four screenshots in `REVIEW/screenshots/style/`; stop and say what is missing if a believable dusk harbor street is out of reach; no endless polish. (2) Guidance: the sketchbook's current page always shows a drawing of the next thing on the main path; after 60 s without progress the sketchbook button pulses once and the book then offers the next hint level; trying the locked drawer makes the key glint within 3 s; a real-click test on the playtest build completes the shop with the sketchbook only. (3) A Ron Gilbert style puzzle dependency chart for all six places in `REVIEW/`, with every stuck point marked. Budget: stop at $50 for the round.

**How the style frame is built (builder's decisions).**
- The world data stays the source of truth. Each street prop gained a `look` (`props.json`): a texture set with a tile size, a glTF model with a fit rule, a built house, water, glass or a plain colour. Positions and sizes did not change except where noted, so the walk map, the openings and the seam are the same as before. `src/render/dressing.ts` reads the looks after the graybox scene exists and swaps materials or hides the graybox shape under a model. Only places with `style: "realistic"` load anything; the other five places are untouched graybox.
- Textures tile by real metres: a box gets six materials so a 30 m wall and a 5 m wall both show the plaster at the same scale. The single ARM file serves as ambient occlusion, roughness and metalness, as Poly Haven packs it.
- Houses are built from their data box: plaster walls, a tiled pitched roof with gable ends, a chimney, a gutter and downpipe, recessed windows with a glass pane, a frame and a stone sill, a planked door with a doorstep, and a few lit windows. The single house rows became seven houses of different heights and plasters.
- Models are placed with their feet on the floor of the prop's box, scaled to the box's height (or its box, with a quarter turn handled). The fish stall is the wooden table under a cloth canopy on four posts; crates, buckets, lanterns, a bench, planters, the ladder, the lifebuoy and the three street lamps are models.
- Light: the HDRI turned so its sunset sits over the harbor (its sun was found in the file at u 0.604), a warm low sun light with a 2048 shadow map on the high tier, filmic tone mapping at exposure 0.5, and a bluish linear mist from 20 m so the quay, the boats and the lighthouse soften. The water is a flat reflective plane with a slowly moving normal map.
- **Tone mapping is per place.** The live pictures inside openings are never tone mapped by Three.js (render targets are not), and fog is applied after tone mapping, so a filmic curve on every place broke the hand-over on the fog-heavy graybox places (measured 5 to 12 on the seam scale). The renderer now uses the filmic curve only in realistic places and none in graybox places, switching at the hand-over with the destination's shaders compiled ahead during the first half of the dive. The seam is back to 0.65 / 3.41 / 0.47 / 0.88 / 3.86 / 0.18. When the shop becomes realistic, its live picture will need tone mapping of its own; noted as the next rendering job, not done now.
- **Believability.** The frames in `REVIEW/screenshots/style/` read as a dusk harbor street: real materials, real shadows, a sunset over the sea, lit windows and a lit shop door. What is still plain: the six usable things and the two hidden things are coloured shapes (a chalkboard slab, a red umbrella beam, an egg for the gull); the headland is a textured block; the boats are planked boxes; the sea has no waves or foam. None of this needed a stop; the founder decides whether it is enough for a style frame.
- The cat on the shop's counter stays a simple shape (change 6).
- **Download and frame rate.** The street loads 37.3 MB in 78 files (HDRI 4.4 MB, 8 texture sets, 12 models, all at Poly Haven's 1k size), measured on the wire by `tools/style_shots.mjs`; it took about 19 s to arrive and decode here. A phone frame rate cannot be measured from this container; the only numbers available are headless software rendering on a 390×844 screen: high tier about 500 ms per frame, low tier (no shadows, no antialiasing, three quarters of the pixels) about 100 to 150 ms per frame, indicative only. Phones pick the low tier automatically (`detectQuality`); `?quality=low|high` forces a tier for measuring. A real phone number is the founder's to read from the frame recorder (`?perf=1`, "Copy frame times"). If 37 MB is too much for phones, the next lever is 512 px textures (Poly Haven offers them) and dropping the two heaviest models (the lifebuoy and the bench, about 2.5 MB each).
- The S1 sketch still shows the lighthouse between two roofs: the middle house on the left was lowered to 4.4 m so the tower shows in the notch.

- **Testing cost of the style frame.** This container renders in software; the realistic street runs at 100 to 1000 ms a frame here, so every real-input test slowed ten times and five timed out. Two product changes came out of it: the low tier now also draws at three quarters of the screen's pixels (a sensible phone tier), and Begin reads "Loading…" until the place's assets are in, so play, and the player's clock, start on a finished picture. The real-input tests run the street on the low tier in a smaller window and wait on frames rather than wall time. The 60 s rule is asserted only when the page runs at device speed (under 50 ms a frame); here it prints the seconds instead (about 80 s on the phone-size run at 90 ms a frame, 120 s on the laptop-size run at 190 ms a frame, harness time). Before the art, the same runs took 26 and 30 s. A real device is the only honest source for this number now.

**Guidance (part 2).**
- `nextObjective` in the rules gives the next main-path object: the next required step's object, else the dive opening, null at the end. The sketchbook's current page is a drawing of it made by the sketch renderer from the object's home spot, zoomed so it fills about a third of the frame. The page names nothing; the player finds it in the world. It is redrawn after each step so an opened drawer looks open.
- No progress (no step, find or dive) for 60 s: the sketchbook button pulses once and the current page carries a hint button for the main-path target, counted as a hint use; progress withdraws it.
- A rattle from a locked thing makes the next main-path object glint 1.5 s later (within the 3 s asked).

**Dependency chart (part 3).** `tools/puzzle_chart.mjs` draws `REVIEW/puzzle_chart.svg` and `.png` from the chain in `SOLUTIONS.md`. Ten stuck points are marked: six red (nothing visible says what to do: the key on the counter before this round's page and glint, the envelope on the letter hill, the feather on the nose, the ear that needs looking up, covering the reflected lamp, the spark in the crater) and four amber (the door glow, the locked drawer, the lamp socket, the edge below the rise).

## D-011 — Fifth round (founder, 2026-10-06): a small complete game of two places for the first strangers

**Founder decisions.** This is the last build round before 3 to 5 strangers play. Scope cut: the playtest build covers the harbor street and the curiosity shop only; diving into the open blue drawer ends the game with a short ending screen ("To be continued") showing the time, the finds and the hints used. Places 3 to 6 stay in the code but cannot be reached on the playtest build. Build now: (1) the scope cut; (2) the next main-path goal always on screen as a small drawing in a corner card that opens the sketchbook, with nothing important depending on finding a button; (3) a find counter ("3 of 12 found") and 10 to 12 optional finds over the two places (about 6 easy, 4 medium, 2 hard), each with an instant reward: a sound and the object flying into the sketchbook; (4) one consistent look, with no flat-coloured placeholder shapes left in the street or the shop; (5) the shop dressed with eight named Poly Haven models, warm lamp light and dusk through the windows, its live picture through the street door matching the real shop at the hand-over (seam check passing); (6) the key on the counter catching the lamp light, and the glint on a locked-drawer rattle kept; (7) 512 px textures wherever the difference does not show, under 30 MB for the two places. Acceptance: a real-click end-to-end run on the playtest build from Begin to the ending screen; counter, goal card and ending screen working with mouse, touch (390×844) and keyboard; unit tests passing; the seam passing street→shop and shop→drawer; five screenshots in `REVIEW/screenshots/round5/`. Stop and report instead if the shop cannot be dressed without breaking the seam, the download cannot get under 40 MB, or a core step needs a hidden button. Cost rules: unit tests freely, the full end-to-end suite once at the end, no visual polish beyond the list, stop after 30 minutes blocked, no scheduled check-ins of any kind.

**How it is built (builder's decisions).**
- **Scope is data, not a fork.** `Scope` in `src/game/rules.ts`: the playtest scope plays `street` and `shop` and ends after the shop; the full scope plays the chain. The playtest build always uses the playtest scope; a dev build uses it with `?scope=playtest` (so the hook-driven tools can look at it) and the full chain otherwise. `endDive` is the scoped build's last dive: allowed exactly where a normal dive is (the blue drawer unlocked), it marks the shop dived and the game ended, and the player stays in the shop. Nothing of places 3 to 6 is loaded on the playtest build: the opening in the drawer shows a soft warm light instead of the next place's live picture, because that place is still graybox and the founder ruled out flat placeholder shapes in the shop. The dive flies into the light until it fills the screen, then the ending screen shows. The dev build keeps the real drawer place behind the opening, so the seam tool still measures the shop→drawer hand-over that the chain will use.
- **Ending screen.** "To be continued", one plain line, the time from Begin to the dive, the finds as "N of 12" and the hints used; "Keep looking" returns to the shop (finds can still be made), "Restart" starts again. The full chain's own ending text is unchanged.
- **Goal card.** A small paper card in the bottom-right corner shows the existing drawing of the next main-path thing (`nextObjective`), made only after the place has loaded. Tapping or clicking it, or Tab then Enter, opens the sketchbook (B still does). It hides during dives, while a panel is open and after the end. On a 390×844 phone it sits right of the lens button and below the pocket.
- **Find counter.** "N of 12 found" under the top-right buttons; it opens the sketchbook too. **This replaces the spec's 24-find count for what the player sees**: the counter counts the optional hidden things of the places the build plays (12 on the playtest, 20 in the whole chain). Sketches and dives are not counted. The reward for a find: the `found` sound, a "Found: …" line, and the find's outline flying in a gold disc from where it was on screen into the sketchbook button, which pulses; the counter ticks up as it lands. A found thing taken with "Take" leaves the world; one only looked at stays and glints.
- **Twelve finds.** Street: a starfish on the cobbles, a toy sailboat in a puddle, a fisherman's hat on a crate (easy); the folded umbrella behind the stall, a green glass float among the rope coils on the quay (medium); the ship in a bottle on a far sill (hard). Shop: spectacles on the counter, a snow globe on the tea table, a brass compass on the back table (easy); the marble on the floor by the chest, a clockwork mouse by the mouse hole (medium); a teacup with a gold star on the window sill behind you as you come in (hard). Easy finds need the lens at 2× from their spot and have a wide hit area; medium 2.5×; hard 3×. Every find has three hint levels and an outline on its place's sketch page.
- **Two unit-test rules changed with this round.** A sketch page now lists every hidden thing of its place (six each in the street and the shop), not exactly two. Spec §5's "at least four ordinary things for every important one" now counts the main path only (steps and dive openings), not optional finds; otherwise twelve finds would force forty-eight decoys. The street keeps at most six ordinary things (D-009).
- **One look.** Objects (not only props) can now carry a `look`: a pack model, one named node of a model, a code-made object from the new kit (`src/render/kit/`), or a textured box. The plain box stays in the scene, unseen, for picking, sight lines and state; the look follows it (wiggle, glint, open/closed). Thirty-seven kit builders make what the pack has no model for, each textured (pack wood and plaster, drawn canvas textures, brass, iron, glass): in the street the umbrella, ship in a bottle, chalkboard, fish scale, gulls sitting and flying, the shop's hanging cat's-eye sign, the notice, the doorbell, the four new finds, rope coils, nets, the striped canopy, the letterbox, the weathervane and the lighthouse lantern; in the shop the key, counter, bell, scales, globe, music box, big book, cash box, the six finds, the sleeping cat, books, jars, framed sea charts and the mouse hole. Lit window panes got glazing bars and curtains; puddles became thin see-through mirrors. A prop drawn as a model now keeps its box for sight lines, so nothing is "seen" through a shelf drawn as a model (before, in the street, it could be).
- **The shop.** Rebuilt around the eight models: the low chest of drawers (`vintage_wooden_drawer_01`) on the right wall holds the blue drawer, which is the chest's own top-middle drawer painted blue (its grain kept in the normal and roughness maps); its other five drawers open and close; the grandfather clock behind the counter; the display shelves with jars; two worn bookshelves with books standing in rows on the model's real shelf heights; two wooden tables, one with the tea set; the mantel clock on the chest; the oil lamp on the counter. Plastered walls, plank floor and ceiling, a front wall with the door and a window. Light: the oil lamp (warm, beside the key), a lantern on the chest (so the blue drawer reads), a lantern on the tea table, a cool dusk light through the front and the dusk sky in the window glass. No fog indoors.
- **Seam with a realistic shop.** Render targets are never tone mapped, so an opening onto a realistic place now applies the screen's tone mapping to its live picture (the quad is tone mapped; one onto a graybox place still is not). The shop uses the street's exposure (0.5) and has no fog, so the picture through the street door is the shop exactly as the screen shows it after the hand-over. Measured by `tools/seam.mjs --only=street,shop` on the dev build: street→shop 0.85 and shop→drawer 0.71 on the 0–255 scale (under about 4 is texture resampling). The first shop→drawer run gave 6.88: the blue drawer's front edge stood 3 cm above the opening and showed as a dark strip at the hand-over; the opening was narrowed by 4 cm and lifted 5 mm. The seam tool also had to freeze the dive in the same call that starts it, since a 2 s dive could end on this renderer before the next call.
- **The key.** Polished brass beside the oil lamp's flame, so it catches the light; the rattle glint (D-010) is unchanged and works on the kit key like on any look.
- **Download.** Every texture set and model now loads at 512 px (`*_512.jpg`, `*_512.gltf`, made by `tools/resize_assets.mjs`; the 1k originals stay in the repo and `?res=1k` on a dev build loads them for comparison), and the HDRI at 1k (`tools/hdr_downsample.mjs`; mean colour unchanged, the sun moved 0.09°). Side-by-side street frames at 512 and 1k differ by about one level in 255 on average; nothing was kept at 1k. **Measured: the playtest build downloads 12.5 MB in 128 files for the street and the shop together** (asset pack 11.6 MB, code and page 0.9 MB, decoded sizes; `tools/download_size.mjs` sums every response body after the page goes quiet, with the shop's eight models among them). Before this round the street alone was 37.3 MB, and that figure left out the 4.6 MB HDRI, which the preview server sends without a size header.
- **Cost of shadows.** The oil lamp casts no shadow: a point-light shadow draws the shop six more times a frame, which the software renderer here could not keep up with, and phones would pay the same.
